topics.name: Simple past tense (was/were, regular and irregular verbs)

questions.rule: old begins with a vowel sound, so we say an old sack.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past tense.
options: Last year, the friend gave them rice.
Last year, the friend gived them rice.
Last year, the friend given them rice.
questions.rule: give is irregular. Its simple past is gave, not gived.

options: Raju is the most youngest of the three brothers.
Raju is the young of the three brothers.
Raju is the youngest of the three brothers.
questions.rule: For one out of three or more, add -est: the youngest. Never use most with -est.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Yesterday shows the past, so use the simple past: bought.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After were very we need an adjective: kind. Kindness is a noun.
honest begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so we say an honest man.
Last week is in the past. The past of make is made.
kind is an adjective. It tells us more about the priest.
apple begins with a vowel sound, so we use an.
The question is about the past (Did), so reply in the simple past: I finished it.

options: Their mother was an hardworking woman.
Their mother was a hardworking woman.
Their mother was a hardwork woman.
questions.rule: hardworking is the adjective, and it starts with a consonant sound, so: a hardworking woman.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct past tense.
options: The friend visited the mother and tell her his plan.
The friend visit the mother and told her his plan.
The friend visited the mother and told her his plan.
questions.rule: Both actions happened in the past, so both verbs are past: visited and told.

options: I will be back in an hour.
I will be back in a hour.
I will be back in hour.
questions.rule: The h in hour is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an hour.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: than compares two things, so use the -er form: much bigger than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Last year shows the past, so use gave, the past of give.

questions.before: The priest gave the rice to the
questions.rule: Before a noun (people) we need an adjective: hungry people.
than compares two things, so use the -er form: heavier than.
sold is the past of sell. Order: who (He) + did what (sold) + what (the rice) + to whom.

chat: What did the shopkeeper do with the old rice?
options: He sell it to his customers.
He sold it to his customers.
He selled it to his customers.
questions.rule: did asks about the past. The past of sell is sold, not selled.

chat: What do you want for lunch?
questions.rule: egg starts with a vowel sound, so we say an egg sandwich.

options: The farmer lent him a unused plot of land.
The farmer lended him an unused plot of land.
The farmer lent him an unused plot of land.
questions.rule: unused starts with a vowel sound, so an unused plot. The past of lend is lent.

options: Priya is more cleverer than her brother.
Priya is cleverer than her brother.
Priya is cleverest than her brother.
questions.rule: Comparing two people with than: use cleverer. Never put more before an -er word.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: A word that describes a noun (crop) must be an adjective: the healthy crop.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The story is in the past (returned), so the priest greeted him.

questions.before: The friend came back after nearly
questions.rule: year starts with a 'y' consonant sound, so we say a year, not an year.
One shop out of all the shops in the town: use the -est form, the biggest.
Adjectives come before the noun. A size word comes before a colour word: a small brown purse.
To compare two things use the -er form + than: heavier than.

chat: Which bag is heavier, yours or mine?
options: Mine is more heavier than yours.
questions.rule: Two bags are compared, so use heavier than. Do not add more before -er.

chat: Describe your new classmate in two words.
questions.rule: After is, describing words are adjectives: kind and honest.

options: All three brothers was honest and kind.
All three brother were honest and kind.
All three brothers were honest and kind.
questions.rule: brothers is plural, so the past of be is were: brothers were.

options: The priest gave an bag of rice to an old woman.
The priest gave a bag of rice to an old woman.
The priest give a bag of rice to an old woman.
questions.rule: a bag (consonant sound), an old woman (vowel sound). The past of give is gave.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Two people are compared with than, so use the -er form: taller than.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The three brothers is plural. In the past, plural subjects take were.

questions.before: Many months passed, but the friend
questions.rule: The sentence is in the past (passed), so the negative is did not + base verb.
an is used before a vowel sound. Only orange starts with a vowel sound.
A past question starts with Did + who + base verb: Did the friend come back?
such an comes before the adjective + noun: such an honest person.

options: I am at the farm with Raju.
I were at the farm with Raju.
I was at the farm with Raju.
questions.rule: last evening is the past. With I, the past of be is was.

chat: Who is the youngest in your family?
options: My sister Pinky is the younger of us all.
My sister Pinky is youngest than us all.
My sister Pinky is the youngest of us all.
questions.rule: One person out of the whole family: use the youngest of us all.

options: This is the most useful book on my shelf.
This is the usefulest book on my shelf.
This is the most usefulest book on my shelf.
questions.rule: Long adjectives take most for the top degree: the most useful. Usefulest is not a word.

options: The wise old man gave each boy a heavily sack.
The wise old man gave each boys a heavy sack.
The wise old man gave each boy a heavy sack.
questions.rule: Describe a noun with an adjective: a heavy sack. each is followed by a singular noun: each boy.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both actions are in the past (sowed), so the crop grew, the past of grow.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: the ... of all three picks one out of many, so use the -est form: the cleverest.

questions.before: Of the two brothers, Ravi is the
questions.rule: For two people, use the -er form: the elder. Eldest is for three or more.

questions.before: He kept back five sacks and
questions.after: the other twenty at the market.
questions.rule: kept is past, so the joined verb must be past too: sold.
the kindest of all picks one person out of a group, so the -est form is used.

chat: I left a sack of rice with you. What did you do with it?
options: I give it to the poor, and they blessed you.
I gave it to the poor, and they blessed you.
I gave it to the poor, and they blessing you.
questions.rule: did asks about the past, so both verbs are past: gave and blessed.

chat: Was the harvest good this year?
options: Yes, it was the most best harvest ever.
Yes, it was the best harvest ever.
Yes, it was the better harvest ever.
questions.rule: good - better - best. With ever we need the top degree: the best harvest.

chat: Do you want a big sack or a small one?
options: A small one, please. It is more lighter.
A small one, please. It is lightest.
A small one, please. It is lighter.
questions.rule: Comparing two sacks: use the -er form, lighter. Never more + -er.
